name: Enforce boundaries with tooling
description: Use crate or project references, dependency-rule linters and architecture tests; documentation alone is not enough.

name: Architecture decision records
description: Record each significant decision together with its context.

name: Test at the seams
description: Fast core tests with in-memory adapters, contract tests per port, and few end-to-end tests.

name: Twelve-factor discipline
description: Keep configuration, logging and process handling disciplined and environment-independent.

name: Observability as a port
description: Structured logs, traces and metrics are a first-class outbound port, not an afterthought.

name: CI as the gatekeeper
description: Format, lint, type-check and test on every change.

name: Reproducible builds
description: Pin the toolchain, remove build paths and timestamps from the output, and rebuild each release on another machine: a build that any party can repeat bit for bit is a build anyone can verify.

name: Verify the published artifact
description: After a release, download what was actually published and check its checksums, its signed provenance and a fresh install, instead of trusting that the pipeline shipped what it tested.

name: Test the documentation
description: Treat documentation like code: one source for each fact, relative links checked in CI, examples compiled or run, and a test behind every claim a README or release note makes.

name: Generators treat their input as untrusted
description: A generator that emits code (shell completions, SQL, configuration) validates names, quotes free text for the target language, and tests the output in the real interpreter, because its input is data someone else wrote.

name: Test the guard
description: A check that has never failed proves nothing: break what it guards on purpose and watch the check fail before relying on it.
